title: Difluoroenol Phosphinates as Versatile Difluoroenolate Surrogates: Synthesis and Applications in Defluorination and Deoxygenative Coupling
citation: Miki B. Kurosawa; Shuhei Shimoyama; Hiroki Tanaka; Kenta Kato; Junichiro Yamaguchi. Difluoroenol Phosphinates as Versatile Difluoroenolate Surrogates: Synthesis and Applications in Defluorination and Deoxygenative Coupling. ChemRxiv (2025). https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-1rklr
contribution: Separately prepared addition product 5A did not form 3A when treated with potassium carbonate at 80 °C, excluding 5A as a productive intermediate under that test. The authors propose Pudovik addition, phospha-Brook rearrangement, and beta-fluoride elimination to form an enol phosphinate and HF; they further propose that HF trapping favors the phosphinate while protonation without a trapping agent gives the difluoromethyl ketone.

title: Difluoroenol phosphinates as difluoroenolate surrogates: synthesis and applications in defluorination and deoxygenative coupling
citation: Kurosawa, M. B.; Shimoyama, S.; Tanaka, H.; Yamaguchi, J. Difluoroenol phosphinates as difluoroenolate surrogates: synthesis and applications in defluorination and deoxygenative coupling. Chemical Science 2025, 16, 13390–13400. https://doi.org/10.1039/d5sc03915k.
contribution: The final article studies P(O)H reagents with RCOCF3, where CF3 is directly adjacent to the carbonyl. Ph2P(O)H/K2CO3 gives a difluoromethyl ketone, while molecular sieves favor isolation of a difluoroenol phosphinate. Higher reagent loading and temperature permit additional defluorination. Strongly electron-withdrawing ketones fail in the reported substrate scope, and a protonated phospha-Brook side product is not a competent intermediate. The authors propose P-centred addition followed by migration from carbon to oxygen and fluoride elimination. The isolated enol products contain C–O–P, not the target vinyl C–P linkage. These observations identify competing pathways and endpoint dependence; they do not demonstrate Ph2PH failure with RCOCH2CF3. Final-version yields and locators are given in Section S2.5.
evidence_role_and_access: Tier 2; primary full text reviewed.
version_relationship: L055 is the preprint of this study. The final journal article has four authors and governs the numerical outcomes used here; the two records do not provide independent experimental support.

citation: Fengxiang Zhu; Huanan Wu; Xiao-Feng Wu. Palladium-Catalyzed Selenylative Alkoxycarbonylation of Alkynes toward β-Selenated Cinnamic Acid Esters. Organic Letters 27(28), 7714-7718 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.orglett.5c02491
contribution: PhSeH is productive in Pd-catalysed selenylative alkoxycarbonylation of phenylacetylene, ethanol and CO: the optimized reaction gives 88% GC yield. Added bases lower the reported yield to 35% with Na2CO3, 33% with EtONa, 28% with t-BuOK and 22% with Et3N; DMF and DMSO give negligible product. Dimethyl diselenide gives less than 5%, whereas PhSeSePh affords the carbonylated product in 91%. These observations show donor-form and condition dependence. Formation of the productive diselenide cannot by itself be treated as catalyst deactivation. The reaction does not test a fluorinated carbonyl electrophile.

citation: Mohammed K. Abd El-Gaber; Ryan M. Herrick; Pranaya Sudhakar; Ashutosh Rana; Brent A. Roach; Jeffrey E. Dick; Ryan A. Altman. Diselenide-enabled photocatalytic hydroazolation of gem -difluoroalkenes. Chemical Science 16(47), 22701-22710 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1039/d5sc04074d
contribution: Diphenyl diselenide improves photocatalytic hydroazolation of gem-difluoroalkenes and is not consumed by a hydroselenolation side reaction under the reported conditions. Benzimidazole affords a CF2-retaining product in 87%, whereas several azaindoles instead form monofluorovinyl products. The authors propose that selenium-derived species mediate photocatalyst regeneration, deprotonation and hydrogen-atom transfer. This is Tier 2 evidence for intermediate fate and fluorination-endpoint selection, with a secondary role in considering competing endpoints. Selenium is a co-catalyst rather than the transferred nucleophile; the study is not a negative test of project PhSeH coupling.

contribution: Installing a 2-phenylsulfonyl electron-withdrawing group on 3-alkylated 3,3-difluoropropenes enabled mild reactions with sodium alkoxides, phenoxides, thiolates, neutral amines, and Grignard reagents; organolithium reagents were not tolerated because of excessive reactivity. In platinum-catalyzed amination of cyclic 3,3-difluoropropenes, cyclic and acyclic secondary amines were compatible, whereas primary amines and allylamine inhibited the catalyst. The organolithium SN2′ reaction was proposed to be promoted by a C–F···Li+ interaction that increases fluoride leaving-group ability, with LiF formation suggested as an additional driving force.

contribution: 2-Nitrothiazole and 2-nitrobenzothiazole react with methoxide, tert-butoxide, and piperidine to produce the corresponding 2-alkoxy or 2-N-piperidyl heterocycles in almost quantitative yields. No anionic or zwitterionic complexes were detected during reactions of 2-nitrothiazoles, even at high initial alkoxide concentration; Meisenheimer adducts were observed instead for 5-nitrothiazole derivatives. The authors propose that the piperidine rate enhancement in weakly polar solvent arises from a substrate–nucleophile molecular complex that is more reactive than free substrate.

contribution: A Pd-IPent-catalyzed reaction of gem-difluorocyclopropanes with enamides constructs multisubstituted N-H pyrroles through cleavage of a cyclopropane C-C bond, two C-F bonds, and a C-N bond; the products were reported in good-to-excellent yields.
